alternative_strategies.name: Relaxed same-fragment (distance 10mm, allow 10% overlap)
alternative_strategies.rationale: Lowering threshold to 10mm (1.25× radius) significantly increases candidates. Allowing 10% source-index overlap retains distinctiveness while being achievable.
alternative_strategies.risk: Partial overlap means some patch geometry is shared — mild label noise.

alternative_strategies.name: Cross-fragment wrong-zone (adjacent fragment, non-contact patches)
alternative_strategies.rationale: Take patch from contact zone of fragment A, pair with non-contact patch of adjacent fragment B. These are hard because they come from adjacent fragments but are geometrically misaligned.
alternative_strategies.risk: Requires contact-zone labels to be accurate (which they are).

alternative_strategies.name: Curvature-similar patches from non-adjacent fragments
alternative_strategies.rationale: Find patches with similar normal_variance/curvature across non-adjacent fragments. These confuse the network because they look similar but never match.
alternative_strategies.risk: Requires computing per-patch similarity without deep features (use geometry stats).

alternative_strategies.name: FPFH-similar patches
alternative_strategies.rationale: Best hard negatives but requires FPFH descriptors from Phase 4 first.

alternative_strategies.name: Symmetry-based (left/right face regions)
alternative_strategies.rationale: Caesar bust may have near-symmetric regions. These are confusing.

recommendation: Use strategy 1 (relaxed same-fragment) + strategy 2 (cross-fragment wrong-zone). These are achievable without Phase 4 and produce genuinely hard negatives.
